 Weather Tomorrow Monday, November 16, 2026: BMKG Places 10 Provinces on Alert for Heavy Rain, Here Is the List
 The weather forecast for tomorrow, Monday, November 16, 2026, indicates the potential for heavy to very heavy rain in several regions of Indonesia. BMKG has issued an alert status for 10 provinces.
 By: Fadhila Nuraini 
 | 
 Editor: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Contributor: Adit Pranata 
 November 15, 2026, 20:19 WITA · 5 min read 
 Photo caption: Heavy rain pours over an urban area. The BMKG has issued an early warning for the potential of heavy to very heavy rain in several provinces on Monday, November 16, 2026. (Illustration/Aktualita.co) 
 JAKARTA, Aktualita.co -  The weather forecast for tomorrow, Monday, November 16, 2026, shows the potential for heavy to very heavy rain in several regions of Indonesia. The Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) has issued an early warning with an alert status for 10 provinces, including DKI Jakarta, West Java, and Central Java. 
 The warning is a point of concern ahead of the start of public activities at the beginning of the week. High-intensity rain has the potential to disrupt travel, cause flooding, and increase the risk of floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. 
 Advertisement 
 Based on the BMKG early warning update valid for November 16, 2026, the regions under alert status are concentrated on the islands of Sumatra and Java. 
 Meanwhile, several other provinces are in the caution category due to the potential for moderate to heavy intensity rain. 
 The public is urged to pay attention to weather developments in their respective regions, considering that atmospheric conditions can change in a relatively short time. 
 List of 10 Provinces on Alert for Heavy Rain on November 16, 2026 
 The daily BMKG early warning for Monday, November 16, 2026, lists 10 provinces in the category of alert for heavy rain to very heavy rain. 
 The following is the list of regions: 
 Aceh 
 North Sumatra 
 West Sumatra 
 Riau 
 Riau Islands 
 Jambi 
 Bengkulu 
 DKI Jakarta 
 West Java 
 Central Java 
 The alert status indicates the potential for high-intensity rain that requires extra attention, especially in areas with a history of flooding, riverbank areas, and hilly regions prone to landslides. 
 However, a province being on the alert list does not mean that all of its regencies or cities will experience heavy rain simultaneously. 
 Rain distribution can vary between regions, depending on cloud growth, wind conditions, and local atmospheric dynamics. 
 Why Did BMKG Previously Mention 8 Provinces on Alert? 
 In the weekly weather outlook published on November 12, 2026, the BMKG actually listed eight provinces with alert status for the period of November 16–19, 2026. 
 The eight provinces were Aceh, North Sumatra, West Sumatra, South Sumatra, Banten, West Java, Central Java, and Highland Papua. 
 However, that list was an overview of rain potential over four days, not a daily warning specifically for November 16. 
 In the daily update available on Sunday, November 15, 2026, there were 10 provinces with alert status for the following day. 
 This difference is important to note because weekly forecasts and daily warnings have different time scopes. Newer information may also show changes in at-risk regions according to atmospheric developments. 
 Other Regions Under Caution for Heavy Rain 
 In addition to the 10 provinces on alert, the BMKG lists several regions in the caution category for moderate to heavy rain. 
 In the Sumatra region, this category includes South Sumatra, Bangka Belitung Islands, and Lampung. 
 Meanwhile, on the island of Java and surrounding areas, this potential includes Banten, the Special Region of Yogyakarta, East Java, Bali, West Nusa Tenggara, and East Nusa Tenggara. 
 For Kalimantan, the caution warning applies to West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan, East Kalimantan, and South Kalimantan. 
 In Sulawesi, regions that need to be wary of increased rain intensity include North Sulawesi, Central Sulawesi, West Sulawesi, South Sulawesi, and Southeast Sulawesi. 
 Similar warnings also cover North Maluku, Maluku, Southwest Papua, West Papua, Papua, and South Papua. 
 Moderate to heavy intensity rain still has the potential to trigger flooding and disrupt activities, especially if it lasts for a long time or occurs when drainage channels are unable to accommodate water flow. 
 BMKG Reveals Causes of Heavy Rain Potential 
 The increase in rain in various regions of Indonesia is related to several atmospheric phenomena occurring simultaneously. 
 In the weather outlook for the period of November 13–19, 2026, the BMKG explained that the strengthening of the Asian Monsoon is also increasing the supply of moist air toward Indonesian territory. 
 This condition is reinforced by the activity of the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) and equatorial atmospheric waves that support the growth of rain clouds. 
 The BMKG also identified the presence of cyclonic circulation patterns and wind convergence in several regions, especially around Sumatra and Kalimantan. 
 The combination of high air humidity, relatively warm sea surface temperatures, and unstable atmospheric conditions can increase the chances of forming high-intensity rain clouds. 
 For the period of November 8–11, 2026, the BMKG recorded quite high daily rainfall in several regions. 
 Central Kalimantan recorded 174 millimeters per day, followed by Riau with 163 millimeters, West Kalimantan with 158 millimeters, Aceh with 150 millimeters, and South Kalimantan with 149 millimeters. 
 This data is the result of observations from the previous period, not a rainfall prediction for Monday, November 16, 2026. 
 Beware of Floods and Landslides When Starting Monday Activities 
 People living in areas prone to hydrometeorological disasters need to increase their vigilance, especially when it rains heavily for a long time. 
 The BMKG reminds that soil conditions that are increasingly saturated with water due to previous rain can increase the risk of disaster if they receive high rainfall again. 
 "Vigilance needs to be increased regarding the potential for floods, flash floods, and landslides." 
 This was emphasized by the BMKG in the weekly weather outlook updated on November 12, 2026. 
 Residents are advised to ensure that water channels around their homes are not clogged, to avoid traveling through flooded roads, and not to take shelter under trees during lightning or strong winds. 
 Motorcyclists also need to increase their vigilance because heavy rain can reduce visibility and make road surfaces slippery. 
 For people living on hillsides, the appearance of soil cracks, sudden murky water flow, or the movement of slope material should be a serious concern. 
 How to Monitor Tomorrow's Weather from BMKG 
 The weather forecast for Monday, November 16, 2026, may still change following the development of atmospheric conditions. 
 Therefore, the public should check weather information based on their regency, city, or sub-district location through the official BMKG website or the InfoBMKG application. 
 Early warning information is also important to monitor before leaving for work, school, or traveling between cities. 
 With 10 provinces in the alert category in the latest daily warning, vigilance against the potential for heavy rain needs to be a concern at the start of the week. 
 Although not all regions are certain to experience extreme weather, early anticipatory steps can help reduce the risk of activity disruption and disaster impacts due to high-intensity rain.
